hints: Look first at the top calibration image. How many 0.1 mm stage divisions stretch across 100 eyepiece graticule units?
Measure a pollen tube in eyepiece units in diagram 2, convert it using your value for 1 eyepiece unit in micrometres, then divide by 4 hours.
walkthrough:
**Calibrate the eyepiece graticule**

First we must find what 1 eyepiece unit really means at this magnification. The stage micrometer has fixed divisions of 0.1 mm.

In the top view, 100 eyepiece units line up with 2 stage divisions. That is $2 \times 0.1 \text{ mm} = 0.2 \text{ mm}$.

**Convert to micrometres per eyepiece unit**

Cells are tiny, so convert mm to micrometres. Remember $1 \text{ mm} = 1000 \, \mu\text{m}$.

$$0.2 \text{ mm} = 200 \, \mu\text{m}$$
$$100 \text{ eyepiece units} = 200 \, \mu\text{m}$$
$$1 \text{ eyepiece unit} = 2 \, \mu\text{m}$$

**Measure growth and calculate rate**

At start in diagram 1 the tubes are essentially 0 units long. After 4 hours in diagram 2 a typical tube is about 10 eyepiece units long.

$$\text{length} = 10 \times 2 \, \mu\text{m} = 20 \, \mu\text{m}$$
$$\text{growth rate} = \frac{20 \, \mu\text{m}}{4 \text{ h}} = 5 \, \mu\text{m h}^{-1}$$

options.A: Correct. 10 eyepiece units equals 20 micrometres, divided by 4 hours gives 5 micrometres per hour.
options.B: Too high by double. This would come from using 4 micrometres per eyepiece unit or misreading tube length as 20 eyepiece units.
options.C: Wrong units. The value 5 is right but mm is 1000 times too large, pollen tubes grow in micrometres, not millimetres, per hour.
options.D: Wrong on both size and units. It doubles the length and uses mm instead of micrometres.
